walkthroughs.body_html:
Physical Chemistry — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Physical Chemistry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Physical Chemistry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many moles of molecules are in 8.0 g of O₂ (Mr = 32.0)?
options: 0.25 mol
0.50 mol
2.0 mol
4.0 mol
ΔH negative
ΔH positive
ΔH zero
ΔH equal to the activation energy

mcqs.q: A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction by:
options: Providing an alternative route with lower activation energy
Giving the particles more kinetic energy
Shifting the equilibrium towards the products
Increasing the temperature of the mixture

mcqs.q: For N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ (forward reaction exothermic), increasing the temperature shifts the equilibrium:
options: To the left
To the right
Not at all
Only if a catalyst is present

mcqs.q: Does a catalyst change the position of equilibrium?
options: A catalyst always shifts the equilibrium in the exothermic direction.
Higher temperature increases the rate because it lowers the activation energy.
A catalyst shifts the equilibrium towards the products, increasing the yield.
No — it speeds up the forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached faster but the position and yield are unchanged.

mcqs.q: Is energy released or absorbed when bonds break?
options: Breaking bonds releases energy, which is why fuels give out heat.
A catalyst always shifts the equilibrium in the exothermic direction.
Breaking bonds always absorbs energy; energy is released when new bonds form, and the balance determines the sign of ΔH.
Bond breaking neither absorbs nor releases energy.

mcqs.q: Why does a small temperature rise increase reaction rate so sharply?
options: Higher temperature increases the rate mainly because the particles collide more often.
A catalyst always shifts the equilibrium in the exothermic direction.
Higher temperature increases the rate because it lowers the activation energy.
Mainly because many more molecules have energy above the activation energy, not just because collisions are slightly more frequent.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Activation energy”?
options: The minimum energy colliding particles need for a reaction to occur; catalysts provide alternative routes with lower activation energy.
When a condition of an equilibrium system is changed, the position of equilibrium shifts to oppose the change.
The heat energy change at constant pressure; negative for exothermic reactions and positive for endothermic reactions.
A state in a closed system where forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations remain constant.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Enthalpy change”?
options: A state in a closed system where forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations remain constant.
The minimum energy colliding particles need for a reaction to occur; catalysts provide alternative routes with lower activation energy.
The overall enthalpy change of a reaction is independent of the route taken, allowing ΔH to be found from energy cycles.
The heat energy change at constant pressure; negative for exothermic reactions and positive for endothermic reactions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Hess's law”?
options: When a condition of an equilibrium system is changed, the position of equilibrium shifts to oppose the change.
The minimum energy colliding particles need for a reaction to occur; catalysts provide alternative routes with lower activation energy.
The overall enthalpy change of a reaction is independent of the route taken, allowing ΔH to be found from energy cycles.
A state in a closed system where forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations remain constant.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Dynamic equilibrium”?
options: The heat energy change at constant pressure; negative for exothermic reactions and positive for endothermic reactions.
A state in a closed system where forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations remain constant.
The minimum energy colliding particles need for a reaction to occur; catalysts provide alternative routes with lower activation energy.
The overall enthalpy change of a reaction is independent of the route taken, allowing ΔH to be found from energy cycles.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Mole”?
options: The minimum energy colliding particles need for a reaction to occur; catalysts provide alternative routes with lower activation energy.
When a condition of an equilibrium system is changed, the position of equilibrium shifts to oppose the change.
The amount of substance containing 6.022 × 10²³ particles; one mole of a substance has a mass equal to its Mr in grams.
The overall enthalpy change of a reaction is independent of the route taken, allowing ΔH to be found from energy cycles.
